headline: AI drug-design company Deep Origin says compounds its software proposed for one target were confirmed in the lab of BioAge Labs, an early step in a longer drug search.
score_reason: Company-sourced early milestone from a press release; score kept.
importance_line: It is early proof that AI-proposed compounds can work in a lab, of interest to drug developers and eventually patients, but both companies are the source and no drug exists yet.
summary: Deep Origin says in a press release that its AI-driven software found several chemically distinct compounds against a new target of BioAge Labs, a company developing drugs for heart and metabolic diseases, in under three months, and that BioAge's own lab has confirmed them. BioAge will now try to improve those compounds, and Deep Origin could earn milestone payments if the work succeeds; the claims come from the companies themselves.
notes: Read the company's paid press release, not FirstWord Pharma's article (blocked, empty text). All claims are company statements.
